page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.3xlarge is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by the KVM hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is allocated 16 virtual CPUs corresponding to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector instruction capabilities, standard AES cryptographic support, and a cache hierarchy containing 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 128 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. No local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this configuration, requiring attached cloud block storage and provisioned networking for persistent deployment. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark measurements indicate a profile geared toward parallel throughput rather than single-threaded execution speed. Single-core performance scores in stress-ng and Geekbench sit in the lower quartile, mirrored by subdued single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression speeds. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale reliably into average ranges, demonstrated by multi-core stress-ng scores of 17,371.73 and Geekbench multi-core marks of 7,731.0. Large-block memory transfers achieve 86.27 GB/s for reads and 48.78 GB/s for writes, enabling consistent execution across larger in-memory footprints. PassMark database tests and Redis operations yield steady intermediate performance, with Redis reaching 21.19 million operations per second and web throughput stabilizing at 11.38 GB/s.

From a cost-efficiency and architectural standpoint, the ecs.e3.3xlarge delivers substantial memory density per core, making it effective when large datasets must reside primarily in RAM without paying for excessive compute overhead. However, the modest clock frequency and low single-core processing capabilities represent an operational tradeoff for jobs with sequential computation bottlenecks. Workloads that match this profile include in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed extract-transform-load jobs, batch analytics, and enterprise web services requiring elevated working memory capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.3xlarge is a memory-focused instance offering 16 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 8 physical cores and simultaneous multithreading, it features a 1:8 compute-to-memory distribution alongside AVX-512 extensions and 33 MB of L3 cache. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying on external volumes, and does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results display modest single-core throughput alongside stable average multi-core and memory subsystem performance, as evidenced by 21.19 million Redis operations per second and steady database processing metrics. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides practical resource density for RAM-intensive jobs, though lower per-thread compute power presents a tradeoff for execution bottlenecks. The instance is well matched for Redis clusters, in-memory database engines, caching tiers, and medium-scale memory-resident data transformation workflows.
